'''Berndt O. Mueller''' (also '''Berndt Müller''') (born 8 February 1950 in [[Markneukirchen]],  [[East Germany|German Democratic Republic]]) <ref>{{Cite web |title=Personal Stuff |url=https://webhome.phy.duke.edu/~muller/PersonalStuff.html |access-date=2025-12-14 |website=webhome.phy.duke.edu}}</ref> is a German-born theoretical physicist who specializes in [[nuclear physics]].<ref name="Duke"/><ref name="BNL"/> He is a professor at [[Duke University]].

==Life==
Müller moved with his mother to [[Frankfurt am Main]] in 1953, where they joined his father. He enrolled as a student at the [[Goethe University Frankfurt]] in 1968 and graduated in 1972. Müller received his doctorate, with [[Walter Greiner]] as his [[doctoral advisor]], in 1973.<ref>{{Cite thesis|title=Die Zweizentren-Dirac-Gleichung|url=https://www.tib.eu/de/suchen/id/TIBKAT:046590722/Die-Zweizentren-Dirac-Gleichung/|publisher=Frankfurt a. M., Univ., Diss.|date=1973|first=Berndt|last=Müller}}</ref> In 1974, he was a postdoctoral fellow at [[Yale University]] and then Research Associate at the [[University of Washington]]. From 1976 he was a professor at the Goethe University Frankfurt. He has been a professor at [[Duke University]] since 1990 (since 1996 as "JB Duke Professor of Physics"). From 1997 to 1999 he was chairman of the Faculty of Physics and from 1999 to 2004 Dean of the Faculty of Natural Sciences. He is a [[US citizen]]. He was, among other guest scientists at [[Caltech]] (1980), the [[University of Cape Town]](1984), the Institute of Nuclear Physics of the [[University of Tokyo]], the [[Yukawa Institute]] of the [[University of Kyoto]] and the [[University of Arizona]] (1987).

Müller is concerned with the theory of [[quark–gluon plasma]] and evidence of its formation in heavy-ion scattering experiments (via enrichment with [[strange quark]]s), but also with chaos in gauge field theories, the [[Casimir effect]], and neural networks.

* 1975 — Röntgen Prize of the [[University of Giessen]]<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=List of Winners of the Roentgen Prize|url=https://www.uni-giessen.de/org/admin/stab/stf/dl/preise/roentgen-preis-en/spreadsheet-en|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200428072311/https://www.uni-giessen.de/org/admin/stab/stf/dl/preise/roentgen-preis-en/spreadsheet-en?set_language=en|archive-date=28 April 2020|access-date=28 April 2020|website=Justus-Liebig-Universität Gießen|language=en}}</ref> 
* 1994 — Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]]<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=APS Fellow Archive|url=http://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200428074642/https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=M&year=2019&unit_id=&institution=|archive-date=28 April 2020|access-date=28 April 2020|website=www.aps.org|language=en}}</ref>

* 2007 — [https://engage.aps.org/sesaps/honors/prizes-awards/beams Jesse Beams Award] from the [[American Physical Society]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://physics.aps.org/authors/berndt_muller|title=Physics - Berndt Müller|last=|first=|date=|website=physics.aps.org|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200428073802/https://physics.aps.org/authors/berndt_muller|archive-date=28 April 2020|access-date=28 April 2020}}</ref>
